The horoscope was right: Ana, Mihai and Kenji have landed in Japan. Kenji’s parents are waiting for them.
Welcome to Osaka! How was the flight?
Very long. We left Madrid fourteen hours ago and I haven’t slept at all.
I have. When we took off, I had already fallen asleep. I woke up as we were landing!
My parents are waiting for us at home. Listen: when you go in, take your shoes off. And don’t worry, they’ll give you slippers.
And how do we greet them? Do we give them two kisses, like in Spain?
No, please! Don’t kiss them. Bow a little and say “Hajimemashite”.
I know that one! I learned it in the app. I’ve been learning Japanese for a year.
I’ve brought a present for your parents: turrón from Alicante. Shall I give it to them when we arrive?
Yes, give it to them with both hands. They’ll love it.
Kenji, what are we doing tomorrow?
In the morning we’re going to Osaka Castle. It’s cherry blossom season now.
How exciting! I had always dreamed of seeing the cherry trees. When I was little, I had a book with pictures of Japan.
And I’d like to try real ramen. Kenji, would you take us to your favourite restaurant?
Of course. But I’m warning you: there you eat with chopsticks and slurp noisily. It’s a sign of good manners!
At last, a custom I’ll be good at!
“me había dormido” = I had fallen asleep
“se me dará bien” = I’ll be good at it
The “vosotros” imperative ends in -d (decid, escuchad), but with a pronoun it loses the d: quitaos, inclinaos (not “quitados”).
Say the long sentence without pausing, linking the words: “Cuando despegamos, ya me había dormido”. Now you can speak fluently!
Salimos de Madrid hace catorce horas.
Cuando era pequeña, tenía un libro.
If the dialogue above seems easy, congratulations: you’ve mastered the Spanish past!
Me gustaría probar el ramen. ¿Nos llevarías?
The golden rule: in the affirmative, pronouns are attached at the end (quítate); in the negative, they go in front (no te quites).
The “vosotros” form is only used in Spain. In Latin America “ustedes” is used for everyone.
Se me ha olvidado el pasaporte.

At B1 the big adventure awaits: the SUBJUNCTIVE (quiero que vengas, no creo que sea, si tuviera…). You’ve already seen it in a few texts. It’s logical, and English has traces of it too (“If I WERE you”, “I suggest he GO”), so it will be easier than you think.
Tip: before B1, spend a week reviewing: daily review + rereading the long texts from chapters 13–36.

The last page of Ana’s travel diary, written on the plane home.
I’m writing these lines on the plane. Two weeks ago we landed in Osaka, and today we’re going home.
Before the trip I was scared: I didn’t speak Japanese and I had never been to Asia.
But Kenji’s parents welcomed us as if we were family.
His mother taught me to make onigiri, and his father took us fishing at dawn.
On the day I saw the cherry blossoms, I cried. It was just like the book I had when I was little.
What surprised me most was the respect: nobody shouts, everything is very clean and people always help you.
Mihai spoke Japanese with everyone. At first people laughed, but then they congratulated him.
On the last evening, in a temple in Kyoto, he told me he had something important to ask me.
He bowed, like the Japanese, took out a little box and asked me if I wanted to marry him.
I told him yes, of course. But first I told him we would tell my grandmother before anyone else.
The horoscope was right: this was the most important trip of my life. And next year there will be two weddings!
¿Qué le enseñó la madre de Kenji?
Al ver los cerezos en flor
¿Cuántas bodas habrá el año que viene?
Mihai had been carrying the ring in his pocket for three months. He had bought it in January, at the same jeweller’s he had recommended to Javier, and since then he had taken it everywhere.
He had often thought about the perfect moment, but it never came.
First he wanted to propose on her birthday, but Ana had flu. Then at a romantic dinner, but the restaurant was closed.
One day, in the Retiro, he already had the ring in his hand when Lucía and Javier turned up. He hid it so fast that it nearly fell into the lake.
Then came the trip to Japan. Mihai thought: “If not there, then never.”
For two weeks he looked for the ideal place. Osaka Castle had too many tourists. The fish market smelled too strongly of fish.
At Kenji’s parents’ there were too many people and too much sake.
On the last evening they went to Kyoto. Kenji had told them about a small temple, hidden on a hill, away from the tourists.
They climbed many stone steps. When they reached the top, the sun was setting and the cherry trees were in blossom.
The pink petals were falling slowly, as if it were snowing. There was nobody else. All you could hear was the wind and a distant bell.
Ana stood in silence, looking at the city at her feet. “I’ve never seen anything so beautiful,” she whispered. “It’s just like the book I had when I was little.”
Mihai knew it was the moment. His hands were shaking more than on his first night shift.
He bowed, as Kenji had taught him, and took the little box out of his pocket.
“Ana,” he said, and his voice barely came out. “Two years ago I walked into a café in Madrid, lost, without speaking good Spanish. I spilled coffee on your book and you laughed.”
“Since that day I haven’t stopped learning: new words, new food, a new city… and loving you a little more every day.”
Ana looked at him. Her eyes were full of tears and she had a huge smile. A cherry petal had fallen into her hair.
“Yes,” she said. “Yes, yes, yes.” And then, laughing: “But this time, don’t spill the coffee.”
They walked down the steps hand in hand as the lights of Kyoto came on. Mihai thought of everything he had lived through since that first “¡Hola!”.
And he knew that the most beautiful story of his life had only just begun.
That same night, before going to bed, Ana called Madrid. Grandma Rosario answered on the first ring, as if she had been waiting for the call.
“I already know,” said Grandma before Ana could say a word. “I knew from the first New Year’s Eve. Congratulations, my dear!”
“el sol se estaba poniendo” = the sun was setting
“cogidos de la mano” = hand in hand

¿Por qué no se lo pidió en su cumpleaños?
